subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs. Competitors
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + proposed bake-off plan (Redwood vs. incumbents)

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High per-user inference cost on peak hours and large batch jobs (billing spikes)
- Latency variability affecting clinician-facing features (95th percentile latency spikes)
- Need for predictable SLAs and clearer audit logs for compliance

Your goals / decision criteria:
1) Latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms for clinical queries)
2) Unit cost reduction vs current provider (target 30% lower)
3) Robust audit logs + SOC2 evidence for PHI handling
4) Smooth rollout with minimal engineering lift (SDK + infra parity)

Competitive context discussed:
- Current incumbent: Acme AI (good accuracy, costs variable during peak)
- Internal PoC with HealthOps (on-prem partner) in parallel
- Decision timeline: expected by end of November, exec review week of Nov 29

Proposed bake-off / test plan (attached: omnihealth-bakeoff-test-plan-20261118.xlsx):
- Two-week parallel test (Redwood hosted vs Acme) using a 1k-query synthetic workload + 500 live-sessions sample
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, KV cache hit rate
- Success criteria: meet p95 <200ms and 30% cost reduction on 90% of test windows
- Access: we’ll provide a test API key + pre-configured prompt templates; we’ll need a short allowlist IPs & an NDA (DocuSign link below)

Open questions you flagged:
- Do we need dedicated capacity or will hosted with reserved burst be acceptable? (you said may prefer dedicated for PHI-sensitive workloads)
- What data retention window is required for audit logs?

Next steps:
1) You: confirm final test cohort and share any redline changes to the test prompts — by EOD Thu Nov 19
2) Us (Ben & Lauren): spin up test endpoints, share API keys & metrics dashboard — by Fri Nov 20
3) Schedule a mid-test sync (Nov 24) and final results presentation (Nov 30)

Attachments: omnihealth-bakeoff-test-plan-20261118.xlsx, redwood-vs-competitors-pricing-summary-20261118.pdf

DocuSign (NDA): https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC-OMNI-NDA

Thanks — I’ll follow up once Ben confirms the test endpoints are ready.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@omnihealth.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed bake-off plan (Redwood vs. incumbents)

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Test cohort: we’ll use 500 live clinician sessions (sampled across 3 hubs) + the synthetic 1k-query workload you suggested. Confirmed by EOD Thursday.
- Data retention: compliance wants audit logs kept for 90 days readable by our auditors; can Redwood support that out-of-the-box?
- Dedicated capacity: for the initial bake-off we’re okay with hosted dedicated burst, but if results look promising we’d likely push for Dedicated (reserved pool) for production due to PHI concerns.

Also, please send a short pricing comparison vs Acme — my CFO will want to see line-item delta vs. current contract. Can you include any one-time on-boarding costs, too?

I signed the NDA via DocuSign (just completed) — thanks.

Looking forward to the test.

— Emma
Emma Stone
VP, Product & Clinical Ops, OmniHealth
emma.stone@omnihealth.com
